# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen`. Edit the command catalog or CLI registration instead. -->

Use `board <command> --help` for interactive help. `--json` is available globally and on catalog operations; direct binary routes accept no extra arguments.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                            |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success.                                                                           |
| 1    | Refused or a blocking doctor check.                                                |
| 2    | Invalid command, arguments, or flags.                                              |
| 3    | A dependency prevented the action; it did not apply.                               |
| 4    | Configuration or installation failure.                                             |
| 5    | The action may have applied; inspect the result before retrying with the same key. |

## Daemon address and caller identity

Catalog commands, `board token create` and MCP tool calls reach the daemon at `BOARD_DAEMON_URL`, otherwise at `http://127.0.0.1:<http.port>` from `config.yaml`. With `BOARD_DAEMON_URL` unset and `config.yaml` missing, malformed or invalid, they stop with `config` (exit 4) before sending anything; the error names both. Set `BOARD_DAEMON_URL`, or fix `config.yaml` and set `http.port`; `board doctor --offline` names what is wrong.

The caller is `SPUR_SESSION` inside a Spur session, otherwise `BOARD_TOKEN`, otherwise the first `.spur-board/token` found walking upward from the working directory. The walk stops at the root of the git worktree (the first folder with a `.git` file or directory, which is still searched); outside git it stops before home. Home itself is never searched, even when it is the worktree root. A token above the worktree root, or in home, is not used: move it into a folder inside the worktree or set `BOARD_TOKEN`.

### `board mcp`

Start the MCP server for an agent on standard input and output. Stdout carries only JSON-RPC.

Each tool call finds the caller: `SPUR_SESSION` inside a Spur session, otherwise `BOARD_TOKEN`, otherwise the first `.spur-board/token` found walking upward from the directory the agent starts it in, stopping at the root of its git worktree, or at home outside git; home itself is never searched.

It reaches the daemon at `BOARD_DAEMON_URL`, otherwise at `http.port` from `config.yaml`; with neither set nor a valid config, each call fails with `config` before any request.

A `version_mismatch` answer means the server and the daemon have different catalogs: restart the agent session so `board mcp` loads the daemon's catalog; if it remains, run `board service restart`.

Register it with Claude Code: `claude mcp add spur-board -- board mcp`. With Codex: `codex mcp add spur-board -- board mcp`.

Arguments: none.

Flags:

None.

Example: `board mcp`

Exit codes: see the table above; setup errors are reported by the CLI.

`--json` — Print JSON output or a JSON error.

Example: `board answer B12 "Target v2." --key answer-PROJ-123-example-1432`

Operation errors: `usage` (exit 2: Run `board schema` to see the expected input and fix the arguments.); `wrong_id_kind` (exit 2: Pass the ID kind the operation expects, e.g. B<n> for a block or a task key for a task.); `forbidden` (exit 1: Check which role may run the operation in `board schema`, or ask the operator.); `not_found` (exit 1: Check the ID with `board status` or `board task <KEY>`.); `not_implemented` (exit 1: Ask the operator to update the daemon to a build with this operation.); `block_not_open` (exit 1: Read the task with `board task <KEY>` to see the current blocks.); `wrong_block_type` (exit 1: Read the block type with `board task <KEY>` and use the operation for that type.); `task_archived` (exit 1: Ask an operator to add the task to the board again if work continues.); `idempotency_key_mismatch` (exit 1: Use a new key for a new command, or repeat the earlier input with the same key.); `identity_unavailable` (exit 3: Ask in your own session, then retry the same command later with its existing idempotency key if it has one.); `starting` (exit 3: Wait until the daemon is ready, then retry the command with its existing idempotency key if it has one.).

### `board unblock`

Close a block: the work is done, a reason is given, or its author withdraws it.

Arguments: `<block>`.

Flags:

`--done [ref]` —
`--reason <reason>` —
`--withdraw <answer>` —
`--key <key>` — Idempotency key for this action.
`--json` — Print JSON output or a JSON error.

Example: `board unblock B13 --done example/web#9 --key unblock-PROJ-123-example-1432`

Operation errors: `usage` (exit 2: Run `board schema` to see the expected input and fix the arguments.); `wrong_id_kind` (exit 2: Pass the ID kind the operation expects, e.g. B<n> for a block or a task key for a task.); `forbidden` (exit 1: Check which role may run the operation in `board schema`, or ask the operator.); `not_found` (exit 1: Check the ID with `board status` or `board task <KEY>`.); `not_implemented` (exit 1: Ask the operator to update the daemon to a build with this operation.); `block_not_open` (exit 1: Read the task with `board task <KEY>` to see the current blocks.); `task_archived` (exit 1: Ask an operator to add the task to the board again if work continues.); `idempotency_key_mismatch` (exit 1: Use a new key for a new command, or repeat the earlier input with the same key.); `identity_unavailable` (exit 3: Ask in your own session, then retry the same command later with its existing idempotency key if it has one.); `starting` (exit 3: Wait until the daemon is ready, then retry the command with its existing idempotency key if it has one.).

### `board --version`

Print the installed package version.

Flags: none.

Example: `board --version`

Exit codes: 0 on success; startup errors are reported by the process.

### `board -V`

Print the installed package version.

Flags: none.

Example: `board -V`

Exit codes: 0 on success; startup errors are reported by the process.
